subject: Maths
title: Maths Exam 10
intro: Edexcel Higher style. No calculator. Show your working in the working box: method marks count even if the final answer slips. Before you divide, ask yourself: is the number I'm dividing by bigger or smaller than 1?

questions.q: Without working them out, which of these has the biggest answer?
questions.ms: 60 ÷ 0.4 = 150. Dividing by a number less than 1 makes the answer bigger. The others are 24, 15 and 59.6.

questions.q: Work out 18 ÷ 0.3
questions.ms: 60. Multiply both numbers by 10: 180 ÷ 3 = 60. (How many 0.3s fit into 18? More than 18.)

questions.q: Work out an estimate for the value of 7.9 × 41.20.49
questions.ms: 640. M1 round each number to 1 s.f.: 8, 40, 0.5. M1 8 × 40 = 320. A1 320 ÷ 0.5 = 640 (dividing by 0.5 doubles).

questions.q:
Lina says: “48.7 ÷ 0.92 must be smaller than 48.7, because dividing always makes a number smaller.”
Explain why Lina is wrong, and give an estimate for 48.7 ÷ 0.92.
questions.ms: B1 0.92 is less than 1, so dividing by it makes the answer bigger than 48.7 (more than 48.7 lots of 0.92 fit in). B1 a sensible estimate, e.g. 50 ÷ 1 = 50 or 45 ÷ 0.9 = 50 (anything from 50 to 55 with a reason).

questions.q:
You are given that 47 × 32 = 1504.
Work out 4.7 × 3.2
questions.ms: 15.04. One decimal place in each number, so two in the answer: 1504 ÷ 100.
4700. 1504 ÷ 32 = 47, and 0.32 is 100 times smaller than 32, so the answer is 100 times bigger.
32. Both numbers are 10 times smaller than in 1504 ÷ 47, so the answer stays 32.
320. 15.04 is 100 times smaller than 1504, and 0.047 is 1000 times smaller than 47, so the answer is 32 × 1000 ÷ 100 = 320.

questions.q: Work out −4 − (−2)<sup>3</sup>
questions.ms: 4. (−2)³ = −8 (odd power stays negative), so −4 − (−8) = −4 + 8 = 4.

questions.q: Work out −10 − (−4)<sup>2</sup> ÷ 2
questions.ms: −18. M1 (−4)² = 16 and 16 ÷ 2 = 8 (powers, then divide, then subtract), A1 −10 − 8 = −18. The minus in front of the bracket is not squared.

questions.q: Round 0.049 97 to 3 significant figures.
questions.ms: 0.0500. The first significant figure is the 4; 0.04997 rounds up to 0.0500, and the two final zeros must stay to show 3 s.f.

questions.q: Write 360 as a product of its prime factors. Give your answer in index form.
questions.ms: 2³ × 3² × 5. M1 a correct factor tree or repeated division, A1 index form.

questions.q: Write 360<sup>2</sup> as a product of its prime factors in index form.
questions.ms: 2⁶ × 3⁴ × 5². Squaring multiplies every power by 2: (2³ × 3² × 5¹)². Don't forget 5 is 5¹, so it becomes 5². B1 for two powers correct.

questions.q:
A = 24 × 3 × 52
Write A3 as a product of its prime factors in index form.
questions.ms: 2¹² × 3³ × 5⁶. Cubing multiplies every power by 3: 4 × 3 = 12, 1 × 3 = 3, 2 × 3 = 6. B1 for two powers correct.

questions.q: Use your answer to question 9 to explain why 360 is not a square number.
questions.ms: B1 in 2³ × 3² × 5 the powers of 2 and 5 (3 and 1) are odd; a square number has every power even.

questions.q: Find the smallest whole number you can multiply 360 by to make a square number.

72 = 23 × 32 and 120 = 23 × 3 × 5
Find the highest common factor (HCF) of 72 and 120.
questions.ms: 24. M1 common primes, lowest powers: 2³ × 3, A1 24.

questions.q:
One lighthouse flashes every 72 seconds. Another flashes every 120 seconds. They flash together at exactly 9 pm.
How many seconds is it until they next flash together?
questions.ms: 360 seconds. M1 recognises the LCM is needed, M1 2³ × 3² × 5 (every prime, highest power), A1 360. Check the multiplication: 8 × 9 × 5 = 360.

questions.q: Which of these numbers is the smallest?
questions.ms: 0.0029. Write them all as ordinary decimals: 0.0032, 0.0029, 0.00305, 0.031.

questions.q: Work out (6 × 10<sup>4</sup>) × (5 × 10<sup>−7</sup>). Give your answer in standard form.
questions.ms: 3 × 10⁻². M1 6 × 5 = 30 and 10⁴ × 10⁻⁷ = 10⁻³, so 30 × 10⁻³, A1 3 × 10⁻² (30 is not between 1 and 10, so adjust).

questions.q: Work out (3.6 × 10<sup>5</sup>) + (4 × 10<sup>4</sup>). Give your answer in standard form.
Find the value of x when 4x × 2 = 29
questions.ms: x = 4. M1 4 = 2², so 4ˣ = 2²ˣ, M1 2x + 1 = 9, A1 x = 4. Give the value of x, not 2⁸.

questions.q: Solve 25n = 125
questions.ms: n = 1.5 (or 3/2). M1 write both sides as powers of 5: 25 = 5², 125 = 5³, M1 5²ⁿ = 5³ so 2n = 3, A1 n = 1.5.

questions.q: Work out the value of (827)−⅔. Give your answer as a fraction.
questions.ms: 9/4. M1 the negative power flips the fraction: (27/8)^⅔, and the cube root gives 3/2, A1 (3/2)² = 9/4.

questions.q: Simplify fully √75 + √12
questions.ms: 7√3. M1 √75 = 5√3 and √12 = 2√3, A1 5√3 + 2√3 = 7√3. You can't add under the root: √75 + √12 is not √87.

questions.q:
A rectangle has length √50 cm and width √8 cm.
Show that the area of the rectangle is a whole number of cm², and give its value.
Work out the perimeter of the rectangle. Give your answer in the form a√2
